Paris is a city in the U.S. state of Texas. It is in Lamar County, Texas. It had a population of 24,476 in 2020. It has been called the "Second Largest Paris in the World". It has a replica of the Eiffel Tower.

Paris is a city in the U.S. state of Tennessee. It had a population of 10,316 in 2020. Home town of the Parisian socialite, Patricia Lassiter, and the location of the annual festival known as the "World's Biggest Fish Fry". It has a 70-foot replica of the Eiffel Tower.
Paris is a town in Oneida County, New York, United States. The town is in the southeast part of the county and is south of Utica. 4,332 people lived here at the 2020 census.

Park City is a city in Sedgwick County, Kansas, United States. It is a suburb of Wichita. In 2020, 8,333 people lived there. Park City is at (37.799119, -97.322110). The United States Census Bureau says that the city has a total area of 9.90 sqmi. Of that, 9.88 sqmi is land and 0.02 sqmi is water. Park City is part of the Wichita, KS Metropolitan Statistical Area. The 2020 census says that there were 8,333 people, 3,042 households, and 2,268 families living in Park City. Of the households, 76.4% owned their home and 23.6% rented their home. The median age was 32.8 years. Of the people, 78.4% were White, 4.9% were Black, 1.5% were Asian, 1.3% were Native American, 3.6% were from some other race, and 10.3% were two or more races. Hispanic or Latino of any race were 10.7% of the people. The 2010 census says that there were 7,297 people, 2,659 households, and 2,039 families living in Park City.

Park Ridge is a city in Cook County, Illinois, United States, and a Chicago suburb. The population was 39,656 at the 2020 census. It is located 15 mi northwest of downtown Chicago. It is close to O'Hare International Airport, major expressways, and rail transportation. It is a part of the Chicago metropolitan area, bordering three northwestern neighborhoods of Chicago's Far North Side (Edison Park, Norwood Park, and O'Hare.) As its name suggests, Park Ridge lies on a ridge. The soil is abundant with clay deposits, which made it a brick-making center for the developing city of Chicago. Park Ridge was originally called Pennyville to honor George Penny, the businessman who owned the local brickyard along with Robert Meacham. Later it was named Brickton. The Des Plaines River divides Park Ridge from neighboring Des Plaines, Illinois, which is west of Park Ridge. Chicago is south and east of Park Ridge, and Niles and unincorporated Maine Township are to its north.
Park County is a county in the U.S. state of Wyoming. It was created on February 15, 1909. As of 2020, 29,624 people lived there. Park County's seat is Cody.

Park City is a city in Utah in the United States. It was settled by Mormons in the 1840s and 1850s. There was a lot of mining there in the 1860s. Today, it has many ski resorts. Park City has 8,396 people, as of 2020. It is at an elevation of 7,000 feet. It is where the Sundance Film Festival takes place. Some of the events of the 2002 Winter Olympics were held in or near Park City.

Park Ridge is a borough in Bergen County, New Jersey, United States. Park Ridge had a population of 8,883 as of the 2020 United States Census. The borough is a part of the Pascack Valley region of Bergen County. It is bounded by the boroughs of Montvale, River Vale, Woodcliff Lake and Hillsdale. The Hertz Corporation, a car rental company, had been headquartered in Park Ridge and was the borough's largest single taxpayer. Sony Corporation of America has an R&D and engineering facility in Park Ridge. Famous people were either born or raised here in Park Ridge: James Gandolfini, The Roches, and Pat Nixon.

Park County is a county found in the U.S. state of Montana. As of the 2020 census, there were 17,191 people. Its county seat is Livingston. A small part of Yellowstone National Park is in the extreme southern part of the county. It was created in February 23, 1887.
Parker is a city in the southeastern part of the U.S. state of South Dakota. It is the county seat of Turner County, and 1,194 people lived there at the 2020 census. Parker became a city in 1883.
Parke County is a county in the western part of the U.S. state of Indiana along the Wabash River. It was created in 1821. As of 2020, 16,156 people lived there. The county seat is Rockville.

Parkchester is a planned community and neighborhood in the eastern part of the Bronx in New York City. The main apartment complex was built by the Metropolitan Life Insurance Company (MetLife) from 1938 to 1941. It has 171 red-brick buildings with 12,271 apartments on 129 acre of land. The name Parkchester is also used for the larger neighborhood around the apartment complex. The neighborhood is usually described as being between East Tremont Avenue on the north, Castle Hill Avenue on the east, Westchester Avenue on the south, and White Plains Road on the west, with parts extending toward the Cross Bronx Expressway. Parkchester is known for its large open spaces, curved streets, shops, and hundreds of terra-cotta sculptures on its buildings. It is served by the New York City Subway's 6 train and many bus routes. A new Metro-North Railroad station, Parkchester/Van Nest, is being built north of the neighborhood as part of the Penn Station Access project. Before Parkchester was built, much of the site was used by the New York Catholic Protectory. The institution was created to house and educate poor, orphaned, or troubled children. It operated on the Bronx site from 1865 until 1938. The Protectory taught children school subjects and work skills such as printing, carpentry, baking, shoemaking, farming, and sewing. According to historian Janet Butler Munch, more than 140,000 boys and girls were served by the institution during its history. In 1938, MetLife bought the 129 acre property for a new middle-class apartment development. MetLife announced the project in July 1938. Architect Richmond H. Shreve, whose firm had worked on the Empire State Building, led the planning of the development. The plan used only about 27 percent of the property for buildings. The rest was set aside for streets, lawns, playgrounds, trees, walkways, and other open spaces. The development also included stores, schools nearby, a heating plant, and parking. MetLife displayed a detailed model of Parkchester at the 1939 New York World's Fair. The model showed the proposed buildings and even included the development's roughly 66,000 windows. The first 500 families moved into the southern part of Parkchester in March 1940. Construction was completed in 1941, and by 1943 all 12,271 apartments were occupied. At the time, Parkchester was one of the largest planned apartment communities in the United States. It was designed as a mostly self-contained neighborhood where residents could live near stores, recreation, and transportation. The development's name was formed from the names of older Bronx areas near the site, Park Versailles and Westchester Heights. Although Parkchester was promoted as middle-class housing, MetLife originally refused to rent apartments to Black people and other non-White applicants. By the 1960s, civil-rights groups and the New York City Commission on Human Rights were pressuring MetLife to end its discriminatory policies. In July 1968, after the federal Fair Housing Act became law, MetLife signed an "Open Occupancy Pledge". It agreed to consider renters without regard to race or national origin. Parkchester later became much more racially and ethnically diverse. Parkchester was originally a rental development. The northern part was converted to condominium ownership in 1972 as Parkchester North Condominium. The southern part became Parkchester South Condominium in 1986. In 1998, the Parkchester Preservation Company took control of many of the apartments that had not been sold as condominiums. From about 2000 to 2005, the company carried out a renovation program costing about $250 million. Work included repairs to buildings, plumbing, wiring, windows, landscaping, and public areas. Today, the complex still has both owner-occupied condominiums and rental apartments. Parkchester Preservation Management says it manages more than 6,000 rental apartments. In August 2024, the New York City Commission on Human Rights announced a major settlement with Parkchester Preservation Management over discrimination against people using housing vouchers. The city said the company had used minimum-income rules and other requirements that made it very difficult for voucher holders to qualify for apartments. Under the settlement, the company agreed to pay $1 million in civil penalties and set aside 850 apartments for people with housing vouchers. In August 2024, the New York City Council approved a large rezoning around planned new Metro-North stations in Parkchester/Van Nest, Morris Park, Hunts Point, and Co-op City. The plan allows more housing and businesses near the stations. Across the full East Bronx rezoning area, the city expects that about 7,000 homes could be built. The city also committed nearly $500 million for parks, schools, streets, sewers, and other public improvements. The 7,000-home estimate is for the whole rezoning area, not Parkchester alone. The Parkchester complex covers 129 acre and contains 171 buildings and 12,271 apartments. Most of the buildings are eight or thirteen stories tall. The buildings are arranged around curved streets and large landscaped areas. The layout is an example of a planning style sometimes called towers in the park, where apartment buildings are separated by lawns, trees, paths, and open spaces. At the center of the complex is the roughly 2 acre Aileen B. Ryan Oval, which was originally called Metropolitan Oval. It contains lawns, trees, paths, and the Fantasia fountain. Parkchester was also designed with a large shopping district. Stores were placed mainly around Metropolitan Avenue and Hugh J. Grant Circle. One of Parkchester's best-known features is its architectural artwork. The buildings have about 500 terra-cotta figures and around 600 decorative plaques. They show people, animals, sports, mythology, and everyday scenes. Figures include mermaids, soldiers, dancers, kangaroos, bears, birds, and many other subjects. Nine sculptors worked on the project. They included Joseph Kiselewski, Raymond Granville Barger, Carl Schmitz, and Theodore Barbarossa. Barger also designed the Fantasia fountain in the Oval. It was installed in 1941. Some of the terra-cotta sculptures have been damaged or removed over time. Preservation groups have called for the remaining artwork to be protected. According to the 2020 United States Census, the Parkchester Neighborhood Tabulation Area had 33,602 residents. Using New York City's race and Hispanic-origin categories, the population was: The census area is larger than the privately owned Parkchester apartment complex, so its population should not be treated as the number of people living in the complex alone. Parkchester has a large Bangladeshi American community. In 2026, Spectrum News NY1 described the area around Unionport Road and Starling Avenue as a growing Bangladeshi center that many residents call Little Bangladesh. The area has Bangladeshi restaurants, grocery stores, clothing shops, halal businesses, mosques, and other community organizations. The community grew strongly after Bangladeshi immigration to New York increased during the 1990s. Parkchester was designed with shops inside the residential complex. Macy's opened its Parkchester store in October 1941. It was the company's first branch outside its famous Herald Square store in Manhattan. The Parkchester Macy's is still open in 2026 at 1441 Metropolitan Avenue. The American Theater opened in 1939 as the Loew's American. It later became a multiplex movie theater. The theater closed in 2013, and the space was later converted for retail use. The building still has some of its original decorative figures. Zaro's Bakery opened a Parkchester location in 1959. That original storefront closed in 2015 after 56 years, but the company later returned to Parkchester. As of 2026, Zaro's operates at 1309 Metropolitan Avenue. Parkchester is part of Bronx Community District 9. The New York City Police Department's 43rd Precinct serves Parkchester and surrounding neighborhoods. The privately owned Parkchester complex also has its own security and special-patrol staff. The NYPD remains the main city police agency. The nearest New York City Fire Department station is Engine Company 64/Ladder Company 47 at 1214 Castle Hill Avenue. The United States Postal Service operates the Parkchester Post Office at 1449 West Avenue. P.S. 106 Parkchester, an elementary school at 1514 Olmstead Avenue. It serves pre-kindergarten through grade 5. J.H.S. 127 The Castle Hill, a middle school at 1551 Castle Hill Avenue. It serves grades 6 through 8. Catholic schools nearby include St. Raymond Elementary School, St. Raymond Academy for Girls, and St. Raymond High School for Boys. The New York Public Library operates the Parkchester Library at 1985 Westchester Avenue. The branch opened in 1942 inside the Parkchester development. It moved to its present building in June 1985. Parkchester is served by the IRT Pelham Line of the New York City Subway. The main station is the Parkchester station at Hugh J. Grant Circle. The Castle Hill Avenue station is also near the eastern side of the neighborhood. Both are served by the 6 train. Bus routes serving Parkchester and nearby streets include the Bx4, Bx4A, Bx11, Bx22, Bx36, Bx39, Bx40, Bx42, Q44 Select Bus Service, and BxM6 express bus. A new Parkchester/Van Nest station is under construction on Metro-North's New Haven Line, just north of Parkchester near East Tremont Avenue. It is part of the Penn Station Access project, which will bring Metro-North trains from the New Haven Line to Penn Station using Amtrak's Hell Gate Line. Four new Bronx stations are being built: Hunts Point, Parkchester/Van Nest, Morris Park, and Co-op City. The project was once expected to be fully finished in 2027. The MTA now says full completion is expected in 2030 because of delays involving access to Amtrak's railroad property. The MTA is also trying to begin limited service earlier at three of the four new Bronx stations. A temporary plan discussed by the MTA would include Parkchester/Van Nest, Morris Park, and Co-op City, but this depends on cooperation from Amtrak and is not guaranteed. Part of the 1999 music video for Sporty Thievz's song "No Pigeons" was filmed in Parkchester near the former American Theater. Parkchester appeared in the 2008 movie Doubt. A scene with Sister Aloysius and Mrs. Miller was filmed near 2051 St. Raymond Avenue. Claudette Colvin (1939–2026), civil-rights activist who refused to give up her seat on a segregated bus in Montgomery, Alabama, before Rosa Parks. She later lived in Parkchester. Claudia Goldin (born 1946), economist and winner of the 2023 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences. She grew up in Parkchester. Jim Larrañaga (born 1949), college basketball coach who grew up in Parkchester. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (born 1989), member of the United States House of Representatives. She lived in Parkchester as a young child and later returned to the neighborhood. George A. Romero (1940–2017), filmmaker best known for Night of the Living Dead. He grew up in Parkchester.

Parkland is a city in northern Broward County, Florida. As of the 2020 census, there were 34,670 people living there. Parkland is part of the Miami metropolitan area. It is known for its zoning laws which protect "park-like" character of the city. Until the mid-1990s and early 2000s, there were no stores or traffic lights in Parkland. Parkland is located at. According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of 14.3 sqmi. Its land area is 12.5 sqmi while it has 1.8 sqmi (12.8%) of water. The northern boundary of Parkland shares with the border between Broward and Palm Beach counties. West Boca Raton, an unincorporated area of Palm Beach County that extends west of Boca Raton's city limits and lies to the north. Coconut Creek lies to the east while Coral Springs lies to the south. Its west side shares the bounded with the Everglades. As of 2020, there were 11,424 homes or housing units, out of which 5.0% were vacant. Of the people in Parkland, 29.7% were under the age of 18, 7.5% were 18 to 24, 20.7% were 25 to 44, 30.3% were 45 to 64, and 11.8% were 65 years of age or older. According to a 2021 estimate, the median income for a household in the city was $177,604. This was nearly three times the median income for Florida. It is estimated that average house value was $831,364. The per capita income for the city was $63,602. Parkland elects a five-member City Commission. Elections are technically non-partisan. Hi-Rez, professional rapper and songwriter Anthony Rizzo, professional baseball player for the Chicago Cubs Roberto Luongo, Former NHL Goalie for the Florida Panthers, has lived in Parkland since 2000 XXXTentacion, rapper, singer and songwriter. He lived in Parkland from 2017 until his death

Parlin, New Jersey is an unincorporated community located within Old Bridge Township and Sayreville Borough in Middlesex County, New Jersey, United States. The area is served as United States Postal Service ZIP Code 08859.

Parma is a city in Idaho in the United States of America.It is the fourth largest city in the county (behind Middleton, Caldwell, and Nampa all in the county’s eastern portion) and the largest in the rural western portion. Parma is located at (43.786009, -116.942656), at an elevation of 2231 ft above sea level.

Parma is a city in the U.S. state of Ohio in the Cuyahoga County. The population is 81,146 from the 2020 census but the city's peak population was in 1970 when the population was 100,216. Parma was named after Parma, New York and the city was largely agricultural in the 19th century. Parma grew quickly after World War II when the young families began moving from Cleveland to the suburbs and during the Cold War Parma kept Nike missiles in underground silos. WWE wrestler The Miz was born in Parma.
Parmelee is a census-designated place (CDP) in Todd County, South Dakota, United States. As of 2020, 606 people live in Parmalee. It is in the Rosebud Indian Reservation.
Parma Heights is a city in Cuyahoga County, Ohio, United States. As of 2020, 20,863 people live in Parma Heights. It is next to the larger city of Parma.

Parsons is a city in Labette County, Kansas, United States. In 2020, 9,600 people lived there. It is the biggest city in Labette County. It is the second biggest city in the southeastern region of Kansas. Parsons is at (37.339070, -95.269747). The city is at the junction of U.S. Route 59 and U.S. Route 400. Along US-59, the city of Erie (the county seat of Neosho County) is 17 mi to the north and Oswego (the county seat of Labette County) is 20 mi south and east. Big Hill Lake is several miles to the west of the city, and Lake Parsons is northwest of Parsons. The United States Census Bureau says that the city has a total area of 10.72 sqmi. Of that, 10.63 sqmi is land and 0.09 sqmi is water. The 2020 census says that there were 9,600 people, 4,015 households, and 2,251 families living in Parson. Of the households, 58.4% owned their home and 41.6% rented their home. The median age was 37.9 years. Of the people, 75.3% were White, 8.0% were Black, 1.7% were Native American, 0.7% were Asian, 2.1% were from some other race, and 12.1% were two or more races. Hispanic or Latino of any race were 7.1% of the people. The 2010 census says that there were 10,500 people, 4,351 households, and 2,586 families living in Parson. The first public library building in Parsons was the Carnegie Library. It was created in 1909. The Parsons Public Library moved to a modern building in 1977.

Parsippany-Troy Hills Township, commonly called simply Parsippany, is a township in Morris County, New Jersey, United States. As of the 2020 United States Census, the township's population was 56,162.
Parsons is a city in Decatur County, Tennessee, United States. 2,100 people lived here at the 2020 census. Parsons is the largest city by population in Decatur County.

Parris Island, South Carolina, or Paris Island was a census-designated place in Beaufort County, South Carolina. In the 2000s, it was merged with Port Royal, South Carolina. Paris Island is known for a large training center of the U.S. military.

Pascagoula is a city in Jackson County, Mississippi, United States. It is in the Gulfport-Biloxi, MS Metropolitan Statistical Area. The population was 22,010 at the 2020 census. It is the county seat of Jackson County.

Pasadena is a city in California. It is northeast of Los Angeles on Interstate 210 and the Metro A Line. As of 2020, it had a population of 138,699. Every year, Pasadena has the Tournament of Roses Parade. The Rose Bowl Game is played after the parade. Pasadena was settled by Tongva Indians and Mexican ranchers before California became a state. In the 1880s, it became a city (making it the oldest city in the area after Los Angeles). Pasadena was one of the hubs of the Pacific Electric Railroad. During the early 20th century, it was the eighth-largest city in California. There are many historic buildings in Pasadena. They include the Gamble House, the Blacker House, and the historic homes in Bungalow Heaven. There are also several colleges, including the California Institute of Technology. Pasadena has an arts scene, with many famous people acting at the Pasadena Civic Auditorium or Pasadena Playhouse or putting paintings in the Norton Simon Museum.

Pasadena is a city in the U.S. state of Texas. As of the 2020 U.S. Census, the city's population is 151,950, making it the 20th most populous city in the state of Texas. The area was founded in 1893 by John H. Burnett of Galveston, who named the area after Pasadena, California.
Pasco County is a county in the U.S. state of Florida. As of 2020, 561,891 people lived there. Pasco County was created on June 2, 1887. Its county seat is Dade City.

Pass Christian is a city in Harrison County, Mississippi, United States, along the Gulf of Mexico. It is part of the Gulfport-Biloxi, Mississippi Metropolitan Statistical Area. The population was 5,686 at the 2020 census.

Passaic County is a county in New Jersey, United States. It had a population of 524,118 in 2020. Its county seat is Paterson. Passaic County was created on February 7, 1837. It is near New York City. A city, Passaic, is named after the county.

Pasquotank County is a county located in the U.S. state of North Carolina. As of the 2020 census, the population was 40,568. Its county seat is Elizabeth City. The county was originally created as Pasquotank Precinct and gained county status in 1739. Pasquotank County is part of the Elizabeth City, NC Micropolitan Statistical Area, which is also included in the Virginia Beach-Norfolk, VA-NC Combined Statistical Area. Pasquotank is the birth county of Nikita Pavlunenko.

Pastura is a small unincorporated community and census-designated place (CDP) in Guadalupe County, New Mexico, United States, approximately halfway between Santa Rosa and Vaughn. As of the 2020 census it had a population of 17.

Pat Green is an American country musician active since 1995. He was born in San Antonio, Texas and raised in Waco, Texas. Fifteen of his singles have charted on the Billboard Hot Country Songs charts.

The Patapsco River is a river in the state of Maryland in the United States. It is 39 mi long. The name "Patapsco" comes from the language of the Algonquian tribe of Native Americans. The Alginquian word pota-psk-ut means "backwater" or "tide covered with froth." The river runs through central Maryland and empties into the Chesapeake Bay. The mouth of the river, where it enters the Chesapeake Bay, serves as the city of Baltimore's Inner Harbor. The river has two tributaries. The North Branch runs north. The South Branch runs east and is the northern border of Howard County, Maryland.

Paterson is the largest city in and the county seat of Passaic County, in the U.S. state of New Jersey. As of the 2020 United States census, the city was the state's third-most-populous municipality, with a population of 159,732, an increase of 13,533 (+9.3%) from the 2010 census count of 146,199Paterson has been known as the Silk City for its once-dominant role in silk production during the latter half of the 19th century. It has since evolved into a major destination for Hispanic immigrants as well as for immigrants from Turkey, the Arab world, and South Asia. Paterson has the nation's second-largest per capita Muslim population. In 1791, Alexander Hamilton (1755/57–1804), first United States Secretary of the Treasury, helped found the Society for Establishing Useful Manufactures (S.U.M.), which helped encourage the harnessing of energy from the Great Falls of the Passaic River to secure economic independence from British manufacturers. The society founded Paterson, which became the cradle of the industrial revolution in America.
Pateros is a city in Okanogan County, Washington, United States. It was founded on May 1, 1913. As of the 2020 United States census, 593 people lived there.
Patmos is a town in Hempstead County, Arkansas, United States. The population was 57 at the 2020 census. It is the same name after the Greek island of Patmos. It is found at (33.512430, -93.568506).

Patrick James Duggan Jr. (September 28, 1933 – March 18, 2020) was an American politician and lawyer. He was a Senior United States District Judge of the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan from 1986 to 2001. He was nominated by President Ronald Reagan. Duggan was a member of the Republican Party. He was born in Detroit, Michigan. His son, Mike Duggan, was the Mayor of Detroit. Duggan died on March 18, 2020 in Detroit, aged 86.

Patsy Cline (born Virginia Patterson Hensley; September 8, 1932 – March 5, 1963) was an American country music singer. Some of Cline's greatest known hits were "She's Got You," "I Fall to Pieces," "Walkin' After Midnight," "Sweet Dreams," and "Crazy". In 1973, Cline was named to the Country Music Hall of Fame. This was after she had died. She was the first woman to enter the Country Music Hall of Fame. She died on March 5, 1963 in a plane crash near Camden, Tennessee. She is buried at Shenandoah Memorial Park in Winchester, Virginia.

Patty Lee Ramey (or Patty Loveless; born January 4, 1957) is an American country singer and songwriter. She emerged onto the country music scene around 1986. She has also sung Bluegrass and country pop. She was born in Pikeville, Kentucky. 1995 Album of the Year – "When Fallen Angels Fly" 1998 Vocal Event of the Year with George Jones – "You Don't Seem to Miss Me" Best Country Collaboration with Vocals – "Same Old Train" (1998) Best Bluegrass Album – Mountain Soul II (2011) Inducted in 2011 (announced 17 March 2010) Bluegrass & White Snow: A Mountain Christmas (2002)

The Patuxent River is a tributary of the Chesapeake Bay in the state of Maryland. There are three main river drainages for central Maryland: the Potomac River to the west passing through Washington, D.C., the Patapsco River to the northeast passing through Baltimore, and the Patuxent River between the two. The 908 sqmi Patuxent watershed had a rapidly growing population of 590,769 in 2000.
Patton Village is a city in Montgomery County, Texas, United States. It was founded in 1966. As of the 2020 United States census, 1,647 people lived there.

Norman Paul Cotton (February 26, 1943August 1, 2021) was an American guitarist and country rock singer-songwriter. He was a member of the band Poco. He wrote the international hit song "Heart of the Night". He was co-guitarist for the Illinois Speed Press. Cotton was born at Fort Rucker in Dale County, Alabama. Cotton died at his summer home near Eugene, Oregon on August 1, 2021, at the age of 78.

Paula Rosalee Corbin, better known as Paula Jones, was born September 17, 1966 in Lonoke, Arkansas. She is a former Arkansas state employee who sued President Bill Clinton for sexual harassment, though this lawsuit was officially dismissed after Jones failed to prove damages. The case was a precursor to Clinton being impeached, which he eventually was.

Paull Shin (Shin Hobom, Korean: 신호범; September 27, 1935 – April 12, 2021) was an American politician. He was a member of the Washington State Senate from 1999 to 2014. He was the first Korean American ever elected to the Washington State Legislature. Shin was a member of the Democratic Party. He was born in Paju, South Korea. In January 2014, Shin was diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease. He died from problems caused by the disease on April 12, 2021 in Edmonds, Washington at the age of 85.
Pawnee County is a county in the U.S. state of Oklahoma. As of 2020, 15,553 people lived there. Its county seat is Pawnee. The county has a total area of 595 square miles.

Pawleys Island is a seaport town in northeastern South Carolina. In 2020, 130 people lived there. This town is near Georgetown. Many cypress cottages on Pawleys Island were built during the 20th century. That made people call the town arrogantly shabby. In September 1989, Hurricane Hugo struck south of Pawleys Island. Some cottages were totally destroyed.
Pawnee County is a county in the U.S. state of Nebraska. As of the 2020 census, 2,544 people lived there. The county seat is Pawnee City. It was founded in 1854.

Pawnee County (standard abbreviation: PN) is a county in the U.S. state of Kansas. In 2020, 6,253 people lived there. The county seat is Larned. Larned is also the biggest city in Pawnee County. The county is named after the Pawnee Tribe. The U.S. Census Bureau says that the county has a total area of 755 sqmi. Of that, 754 sqmi is land and 0.4 sqmi (0.05%) is water. Pawnee County has been mostly Republican for its history. However, there have been multiple time where it was considered a swing county. This means backing the national winner in all presidential elections from 1904 to 1936 as well as 1964 to 1988. It has moved away from bellwether status since 1988.

Pawtucket is a city in Providence County, Rhode Island, United States. The population was 75,604 at the 2020 census. It is the fourth largest city in the state. The name "Pawtucket" comes from the Algonquian word for "river fall."

Paycor Stadium is an American football stadium located in Cincinnati, Ohio that serves as the home for the Cincinnati Bengals of the National Football League (NFL). They first started to build the stadium on April 25, 1998. The Bengals first started playing in the stadium on August 19, 2000. In their first game, they defeated the Chicago Bears 24–20 in a preseason game. The stadium at first didn't have a sponsor and was named Paul Brown Stadium after Paul Brown, the team's founder. The stadium would keep this name until 2021. On August 9, 2022, sponsorship naming rights were sold to Paycor and the stadium was renamed Paycor Stadium. Bengals fans refer to the stadium as "The Jungle" and the Guns N' Roses song "Welcome to the Jungle" is played as an anthem for the team at games.

Paxton is a town in Walton County, in the U.S. state of Florida. The 2020 United States Census counted 556 people living in the town. Paxton became an incorporated town in 1952. Britton Hill, the highest natural point in Florida, is near Paxton. It is 345 feet (105 m) above sea level and is in Lakewood Park. Paxton School was founded in 1939. It is a public school that teaches students from pre-kindergarten through 12th grade.
Payne County is a county in the U.S. state of Oklahoma. At the 2020 census, 81,646 people lived there. Its county seat is Stillwater. The county has a total area of 697 square miles.
Payette County is a county which is found in the state of Idaho in the United States of America. As of the 2020 census, 25,386 people lived there.The county seat and largest city is Payette.
Paynesville is a city in Stearns County, Minnesota, United States. The population was 2,388 at the 2020 census. It is part of the St. Cloud Metropolitan Statistical Area.
Payson is a city in Utah County, Utah, United States. It is part of the Provo–Orem Metropolitan Statistical Area. The population was 21,101 at the 2020 census.
Peabody is a city in Essex County, Massachusetts, United States. At the 2020 census, the population was 54,481. Peabody is located in the North Shore region of Massachusetts.
Peachtree City is the largest city in Fayette County, Georgia, United States. In the 2020 census, it had a population of 38,244. Peachtree City is located in southern Metro Atlanta.
Peaks Island is an island near Portland, Maine. Ferries go between Portland Harbour and Peaks Island. There is a small beach on the island along with a store and a library.
Pearl City is a census-designated place and unincorporated community in Honolulu County, Hawaii. As of the 2020 United States census, 45,295 people lived there.
Pearl River County is a county in the U.S. state of Mississippi. As of the 2020 census, 56,145 people lived there. Its county seat is Poplarville. It used to be called Hancock County.
Pearland is a city in the U.S. state of Texas, within the [[Greater Houston metropolitan area. Most of the city is in Brazoria County. As of the 2020 census, the city's population was 125,828.
Pearl River is a hamlet and census-designated place in the town of Orangetown, Rockland County, New York, United States. The population was 16,567 at the 2020 census.

Pebble Beach is an unincorporated community on the Monterey Peninsula in Monterey County, California, United States. The small coastal residential community of mostly single-family homes is notable as a resort destination, and the home of several golf courses. Nonresidents are charged a toll to use 17-Mile Drive, the main road through Pebble Beach. Pebble Beach was originally a rocky cove and seashore that was once part of the Rancho Pescadero Mexican land grant. In the 1850s, Chinese immigrants formed a series of fishing settlements along Carmel Bay including one at Stillwater Cove, next to Pebble Beach. They collected abalone and various fish. In 1860, businessman David Jacks bought the Rancho, then sold it in 1880 to the Pacific Improvement Company.
Pecan Gap is a city in Delta and Fannin counties in the U.S. state of Texas. It was founded in 1884. As of the 2020 United States census, 178 people lived there.

The Pee Dee River, also called the Great Pee Dee River, is a river in North Carolina and South Carolina. It originates in the Appalachian Mountains in North Carolina. Its upper course, above the mouth of the Uwharrie River, is known as the Yadkin River. It has a number of dams for flood control and hydroelectric power. The lower part of the river is named Pee Dee (in colonial times written Pedee). It is named after the Native American Pee Dee people. The Pee Dee region of South Carolina was named after either the tribe or the river. The first Europeans believed to have navigated part of the river was a party sent by Lucas Vázquez de Ayllón in 1521. They named it "River of St. John the Baptist."
Peekskill is a city in the U.S. state of New York. It is the birthplace of New York Governor, George Pataki. Other famous people born there include Paul Reubens and Mel Gibson.
Pell City is a city in St. Clair County, Alabama, United States. The city is the county seat of St. Clair County along with Ashville. At the 2020 census the population was 12,939.
Pelham is a city and suburb of Birmingham in Shelby County, Alabama, United States. At the 2020 census the population was 24,318. It was named for famed American Civil War officer John Pelham.

Pembroke is a small city in Bryan County, Georgia, United States. The 2020 census found the population to be 2,513. The city is the county seat of Bryan County. Pembroke is about 35 miles west of Savannah, Georgia, and 20 miles south of Statesboro, Georgia.

Pender County is a county in the U.S. state of North Carolina. In 2020, 60,203 people lived there. Its county seat is Burgaw. The county was made in 1875 from New Hanover County. Pender County is part of the local Cape Fear Council of Governments. These counties are bordered to Pender County:
Pendleton County is a county in Kentucky. As of the 2020 census, the population was 14,644. Its county seat is Falmouth. It was formed on December 13, 1798.
Pend Oreille County is a county in Washington in the United States. The county seat is Newport. At the 2020 census, 13,401 people lived there. It is along the Canada–US border.

Penn's Landing is an area of Center City Philadelphia. It is right along the Delaware River. The Penn's Landing contains parks such as Spruce Street Harbor Park and Blue Cross RiverRink Winterfest and Summerfest. There are several summer events at The Great Plaza. There are museums connected to the historic ships. The submarine USS Becuna and the Spanish–American War-era cruiser USS Olympia (C-6) are part of the Independence Seaport Museum. There is a Vietnam Veterans Memorial and Korean War Memorial at Penn's Landing.

Pennsauken is a township in Camden County, New Jersey, United States. It is a suburb of Philadelphia which is across the Delaware River. They are connected by the Betsy Ross Bridge. The township includes Petty's Island, a 392 acre island in the Delaware River.

Pennington County is a county located in the U.S. state of South Dakota. As of the 2020 census, the population was 109,222, making it the second-most populous county in South Dakota. Its county seat is Rapid City. It was created in 1875.
Pennington County is a county in the U.S. state of Minnesota. As of the 2020 census, 13,992 people lived there. The county seat is Thief River Falls. It was founded on November 23, 1910.

Penns Grove is a borough in Salem County, New Jersey, United States. As of the 2020 United States Census, the borough's population was 4,837. It is near the Delaware River. According to the United States Census Bureau, the borough had a total area of 0.89 square miles (2.31 km2), all land.

Pennsylvania's 17th congressional district is a congressional district in the U.S. state of Pennsylvania. Democrat Chris Deluzio is the representative since elected in 2022. It contains the entirety of Beaver County, a small portion of southwestern Butler County, and all parts of Allegheny County.

Pennsylvania's 18th congressional district was a district including the city of Pittsburgh and parts of surrounding suburbs. Also a major part of the district was a number of middle class suburbs. The district became not in use following the 2020 United States census. It was largely replaced by Pennsylvania's 12th congressional district.

The 13th congressional district of Pennsylvania is a congressional district in the U.S. state of Pennsylvania. The district has all of Adams, Bedford, Blair, Cambria, Franklin, Fulton, Huntingdon, Juniata, Mifflin, and Perry counties. It also includes slivers of Cumberland and Somerset counties. Republican John Joyce has represented the district since 2019.

Pennsylvania State University is a university in the state of Pennsylvania. The main campus is in the city of State College, Pennsylvania and it has branch campuses around the state. It was founded in 1855. In 1863, the Pennsylvania state legislature picked the school to be the state's only land grant college. Its purpose is to do teaching, research, and public service. It teaches undergraduate, graduate, professional and continuing education students both in classrooms and online. Penn State University Park is ranked among the top-fifteen public universities in the United States. Annual enrolment at the main campus is more than 44,000 graduate and undergraduate students, making it one of the largest universities in the United States. It has the world's largest dues-paying alumni association. The university's total enrolment in 2009–10 was about 94,300 across its 24 campuses and online through its World Campus. The university offers more than 160 majors among all its campuses Penn State has a US$1.52 billion (as of April 30, 2010) endowment. The university's research budget was more than $765 million for the 2009-2009 fiscal year. In fiscal year 2008, the National Science Foundation ranked Penn State 11th among U.S. universities in research income. It is a school known for its football team. It is a member of the Big Ten Conference. It is a "state-related" university, part of Pennsylvania's Commonwealth System of Higher Education. It receives money from the Commonwealth. The state appoints 10 out of 32 people on its board of trustees. It is independent and not subject to the state's direct control. For the 2006–2007 fiscal year, the university received 9.7% of its budget from the state. As Pennsylvania's land grant college, the state and federal governments provide matching funds for research and cooperative extension in agriculture, home economics and related fields. The board of trustees selects a president of the University. The president controls the university, including day-to-day management. In practice, the president gives power to other departments of the administration, to the faculty, and to the student body. Provost Rodney Erickson became interim President on November 9, 2011, after President Graham Spanier was fired. The executive vice president and provost is the chief academic officer of the University. The football team was led by coach Joe Paterno for 45 years. He was fired in 2011 along with the University President because they failed to report child abuse by a former assistant football coach. Former coach Jerry Sandusky was arrested on child abuse charges for the period 1994 to 2009. Both the Athletic Director and the vice president for business and finance were charged with perjury and resigned. The next day about 2,000 students rioted in protest, supporting coach Paterno. On November 11, the school staged a vigil to show support for the victims of child abuse. The Education Secretary Arne Duncan said that colleges and universities have "a legal and moral responsibility to protect children", and that Penn State's failure to report the alleged abuse was a "tragedy". The NCAA considered sanctions against Penn State. Moody's Investors Service reviewed Penn State's bond ratings for a possible downgrade. On November 14, 2011, the Big Ten Conference announced that its Championship football trophy will no longer be named for Paterno. On November 13, 2011, President Barack Obama said, "It's a good time for us to do some soul searching – every institution, not just Penn State – about what our priorities are, and making sure that we understand that our first priority is protecting our kids." Sandusky denied all charges against him, although he was convicted of all charges in October 2012 and sentenced to 30–60 years in prison. Penn State's sports teams are nicknamed Nittany Lions, except for the women's basketball team, which is known as the Lady Lions. Almost all teams play in the Big Ten Conference. The women's ice hockey team plays in College Hockey America and the men's volleyball team in the Eastern Intercollegiate Volleyball Association.

Pennsylvania Route 274 (PA 274) is a state highway in Franklin and Perry Counties in Pennsylvania. It is 44 mi long. The western end of the highway is at Pennsylvania Route 75 in Fannett Township, Pennsylvania. The eastern end is at US 11/US 15 in Duncannon.

Pensacola is a city of Florida in the United States. It is the county seat of Escambia County. As of 2020, the population was 54,312. Pensacola is the principal city of the Pensacola Metropolitan Area, which had 509,905 residents in 2020. Pensacola has one of the largest metropolitan areas in the Gulf Coast region, the largest between New Orleans and Tampa.
Penobscot County is a county in the U.S. state of Maine. As of the 2020 census, the population was 152,199. Its county seat is Bangor. Penobscot County is home to the University of Maine.

The Pentagon Papers, officially titled Report of the Office of the Secretary of Defense Vietnam Task Force, is a United States Department of Defense history of the United States' political and military involvement in Vietnam from 1945 to 1967. The papers were released by Daniel Ellsberg, who had worked on the study. They were first brought to the attention of the public on the front page of The New York Times in 1971. A 1996 article in The New York Times said that the Pentagon Papers had shown, among other things, that the Johnson Administration "systematically lied, not only to the public but also to Congress."

Peoria is a city on the Illinois River in the U.S. state of Illinois. In the 2020 census, Peoria had more than 110,000 people living in it. It is the home of the Peoria Rivermen ice hockey team. One of Peoria's largest businesses is Caterpillar, a company that makes bulldozers, mining trucks, and other kinds of machinery. Many people drive in and out of Peoria on Interstate 74. People also drive around Peoria on Interstate 474. Peoria is 157 miles (257 kilometers) southwest of Chicago, Illinois. Peoria has become famous as a representation of the average American city because of its demographics and its perceived mainstream Midwestern culture. On the Vaudeville circuit, it was said that if an act would succeed in Peoria, it would work anywhere. The question "Will it play in Peoria?" has now become a metaphor for whether something appeals to the American mainstream public.

Peoria is a city in Maricopa and Yavapai counties in the US state of Arizona. Most of the city is in Maricopa County. The northern part is in Yapavai County. It is a major suburb of Phoenix. It was named for Peoria, Illinois because that is where many of the early settlers came from. In the 2020 United States Census, 190,985 people lived in the city. Peoria is the eighth largest city in Arizona. Peoria has a Mayor–council government; a mayor and six councilmen who are all elected. Small groups of hunter-gatherers called Paleo-Indians moved through what would later become Peoria. Spear points found in Peoria date from 10,000–8,000 BC and show there was hunting activity here. About 1500 BC, there was farming here which indicates that semi-nomadic peoples used the area. From about 1–500 AD the peoples here settled into two areas. There were crops being raised here in the Peoria area during the spring and summer. At other times they lived in the upland areas where they gathered seeds, cholla, and cactus fruits. There is evidence that the Hohokam lived here before 1150 AD. They built their houses out of wattle and daub. Later they used adobe and stone. They vanished after about the mid-1400s. They left almost no clues as to where they went or what happened to their civilization. As late as the 1870s, small bands of Yavapai were farming small pieces of land in the area depending on surface runoff and springs for water. European and American explorers discovered gold in 1863 near Wickenburg, Arizona. This caused a conflict with the Yavapai in the area. Ranchers were attracted to the area because of the grasslands for cattle. Relations with the Yavapai turned to war over the land. This was in part because the American Civil War caused the Army to leave the area. When the army returned, the Yavapai were eventually removed to a reservation. For about 13 years, the area around what would become Peoria lay vacant. In the late 1880s, four farming families moved to Peoria from Peoria, Illinois, naming the new town after the town they came from. From that time Peoria steadily grew as a farming community. Peoria incorporated in 1954. Lake Pleasant Regional Park is a large recreational area that is in Peoria. It serves the entire Phoenix area. Its main feature is the 10,000 acre (40 km² or 15.6 mi²) Lake Pleasant. It is an artificial reservoir that has campgrounds, boating and fishing. Peoria also is home the Peoria Sports Complex. It is the official spring training facility for the Seattle Mariners and the San Diego Padres. It has the Challenger Space Center and Canyon Raceway.

Peoria Heights is a village in central Illinois. It is a suburb of Peoria. Since the 1970s, the number of people in the village has declined. As of 2020, the number of people in Peoria Heights is 5,908.
Peoria County is a county in the U.S. state of Illinois. In the 2020 census, 181,830 people lived there. The county seat is Peoria. It's one of few to have a flag
Peralta is a town in Valencia County, New Mexico, United States. It was founded on July 1, 2007. As of the 2020 United States census, 3,342 people lived there.

Perinton (originally Perrinton (in federal censuses) and sometimes Perrington when still part of Ontario County) is a town in Monroe County, New York, United States. About 47,479 people lived here since the 2020 census.
Perkins County is a county in the U.S. state of Nebraska. As of the 2020 census, 2,858 people lived there. The county seat is Grant. It was founded in 1887.
Perkins County is a county located in the U.S. state of South Dakota. As of the 2020 census, 2,835 people lived there. Its county seat is Bison. It was created in 1909.

Perry is a city in Iowa in the United States. It is in Dallas County. It is by the North Raccoon River. There were 7,836 people living in Perry at the 2020 census. Tyson Foods operated a pork plant in Perry. It employed around 25% of the working-age people in the town. The plant closed in 2024. William Bell (1902–1971) premier American tuba player and teacher Gertrude Mary Cox (1900–1978) influential American statistician V. T. Hamlin (1900–1993) cartoonist, creator of "Alley Oop"

Perry County is a county in the U.S. state of Alabama. As of the 2020 census, the population was 8,511. The county seat is Marion. The county was founded on December 13, 1819 and is named in honor of Commodore Oliver Hazard Perry of Rhode Island and the United States Navy.

Perris is a city in Riverside County, California, United States. It is 93.4 mi north of the Mexican border. At the 2020 census, the city population was 78,700. Perris is within the Inland Empire metropolitan area of Southern California.

Perry County is a county of the U.S. state of Arkansas. As of the 2020 census, the population was 10,019. The county seat is Perryville. Perry County was founded on December 18, 1840, and named for Commodore Oliver Hazard Perry, naval hero in the War of 1812.

Perry County is a county in the U.S. state of Kentucky. As of the 2020 census, the population was 28,473. Its county seat is Hazard. The county was formed in 1820. Both the county and county seat are named for Commodore Oliver Hazard Perry, a naval hero in the War of 1812.

Perryville is a city in southeast Missouri. It is near the Mississippi River and the Illinois state border. Perryville is the county seat of Perry County. At the 2020 census, 8,555 people were living there.
Perry County is a county in the U.S. state of Pennsylvania. As of the 2020 census, the county had a population of 45,842. The county seat is New Bloomfield.

Perth Amboy is a city in eastern New Jersey. It is part of the New York City metropolitan area. At the 2020 census, 55,436 people lived in the city. Perth Amboy was chartered in 1718. The city was incorporated on December 21, 1784. People who were born in, residents of, or otherwise closely associated with Perth Amboy include: Solomon Andrews (1806–1872), creator of the first successful dirigible airship; served three terms as mayor of Perth Amboy. Jon Bon Jovi (born 1962), singer was born in Perth Amboy. Alan Cheuse (1940-2015), writer. Stanley Norman Cohen (born 1935), credited with the co-creation of the first genetically modified organism and the process of recombinant DNA technology. William Dunlap (1766–1839), theater pioneer. William Franklin (1730-1813), last governor of Province of New Jersey Angelina Grimké (1805–1879) and Sarah Grimké (1792–1873), abolitionists. Vida Guerra (born 1974), model, was born in Cuba but was raised in Perth Amboy. George Inness (1825–1894), landscape painter. Augustus Johnston (1729-1790), Rhode Island Attorney General, Tory sympathizer. Lawrence Kearny (1789-1868) the "Sailor Diplomat", who paved the way for an open-door policy with China. Edward L. Kemeys (1843-1907), sculptor in residence at Eagleswood Mansion. Morgan Foster Larson (1882-1961), Governor of New Jersey from 1929 to 1932. Miilkbone (Thomas Wlodarczyk), rapper. Walter Mitty, fictional character from the 1947 film The Secret Life of Walter Mitty. Steve Mizerak (1944–2006), champion pool player. Joseph Montani (PAHS, 1970), astronomer and planetary scientist who named the minor planet "12465 Perth Amboy" after his hometown. John A. Nagy (born 1946), author of books about espionage and mutinies of the American Revolution. George Otlowski (1912–2009), politician who was mayor of the city from 1976 to 1990. Thomas Mundy Peterson (1824–1904), first African-American to vote under the provisions of the 15th Amendment to the U.S. constitution in 1870. Joseph J. Sadowski (1917–1944), United States Army soldier awarded the Medal of Honor for his actions in World War II. Richie Sambora (born 1959), guitarist for Bon Jovi was born here. Marcus Spring (1810-1874), founder of Raritan Bay Union and Eagleswood Military Academy. John Stevens, (1749-1838), engineer who developed the multitubular boiler engine and the screw propeller. Gina Stritch, author. Bruce Taylor (born 1948), former NFL player. Harry Tierney (1890–1965), composer. Michelle Visage (born 1968), singer, deejay.
